findings.title: Straddles are priced and marked at VIX (a variance-swap rate), not ATM implied vol; fixing this wipes out S1's profit
findings.description: _simulate_straddle_pnl prices the entry straddle and every daily mark with sigma = _interp_atm_iv(VIX term structure). But VIX is not ATM vol. It is the model-free 30d variance-swap rate, which contains the skew/convexity premium and sits structurally above ATM IV. For a delta-hedged straddle, P&L ≈ Σ½ΓS²(σ_imp² − σ_real²)dt, so using VIX as σ_imp books the skew premium as if an ATM straddle earns it. That inflates every short-vol result and penalises every long-vol one. The README and article call this 'VIX-ATM vol' and disclose only 'no smile'; they never say that the vol level itself is biased. The headline narrative depends on it: the 'C18 inversion centrepiece' (S1 is a profitable short-VRP harvester, so S1C is the artifact) holds only at a ratio of about 1.0 and flips sign at the ratio the project's own option data shows.
findings.evidence: (1) Measured from the project's own SPX option snapshots (options_snapshots): nearest-to-spot IV at 10-60d, interpolated in total variance to 30d, against same-session ^VIX. 2026-03-24: ATM30 22.56 vs VIX 26.95 (ratio 0.837). 2026-03-27: 25.78 vs 31.05 (0.830). 2026-05-29: 13.84 vs 15.32 (0.903). 2026-06-18: 13.86 vs 16.40 (0.845). (2) Sensitivity re-run of the real engine, monkeypatching backtest_engine._interp_atm_iv to f×VIX-interp (scratchpad/bt/sens_vix.py). f=1.00: portfolio −$261,206, Sharpe −1.80, S1 +$693,938, S1C −$599,995, S4 −$206,437. f=0.90: portfolio −$172,324, Sharpe −1.23, S1 +$36,459, S1C −$339,832, S4 −$199,954. f=0.86: portfolio −$135,506, Sharpe −1.01, S1 −$232,561, S1C −$236,003. (3) S1 trade log: mean σ_entry (VIX-interp) 17.0% vs mean realised vol over the trade 15.2%. Scaled to ATM (×0.85 ≈ 14.5%), implied is below realised, so there is no VRP edge. Literature agrees: fair variance-swap vol exceeds ATM IV by an amount set by skew (Carr & Lee, 'Realized Volatility and Variance: Options via Swaps'; CBOE VIX methodology).
findings.proposed_fix: Price and mark ATM straddles with an ATM-vol proxy, not raw VIX. Minimum option: sigma_atm = beta × VIX-interp, with beta estimated from real ATM-vs-VIX data. The 4 in-DB snapshots give about 0.85. Better: fit beta against a free history of 30d ATM IV (e.g., CBOE VIX-decomposition data, or SPY ATM IV if obtainable), possibly regressed on SKEW or VIX level. Make beta a documented BacktestEngine parameter (ATM_TO_VIX_RATIO). Publish a sensitivity table (beta ∈ {1.0, 0.9, 0.85}) in the README next to the headline, and rewrite the C18 'S1 is profitable' narrative, which does not survive beta ≤ 0.9. Test: a unit test that _simulate_straddle_pnl uses the ATM-mapped vol (inject a vix_row and assert sigma_entry == beta×VIX), plus a regression test pinning the sensitivity table.

findings.title: 'Sharpe (vs ^IRX) −1.80' subtracts the T-bill rate from a NAV that never earns interest; the real figure is about −1.14 to −1.19
findings.description: NAV is cap + cumsum(option P&L). The $1M collateral earns nothing, and neither does the premium received on shorts, so the return series is an unfunded (excess) return. compute_metrics then subtracts the per-date ^IRX rate from it again, penalising the strategy twice for cash. The C21 fix, which replaced the stub hurdle with real ^IRX, made this double count larger. The result: the portfolio Sharpe is overstated in magnitude by about 0.6. S3 (+$23K, 73% winners) gets a Sharpe of −5.6. The dashboard explains S3's figure as 'mostly flat NAV → near-zero std → ratio diverges', which is wrong: the number is driven entirely by −rf/252 on idle cash. Cumulative return and NAV also leave out about $150K of collateral interest.
findings.evidence: Re-computed from data_store/backtest/full_results.parquet with the engine's own compute_metrics and ^IRX series (mean 2.40%/yr over the window; portfolio ann. vol 3.63%). Portfolio: published −1.799; rf=0 gives −1.144; NAV accruing ^IRX on cash then minus ^IRX gives −1.190 (end NAV $892,364, cum −10.8%, not −26.1%). S3: −5.605 → +0.903 (rf=0) / +0.899 (funded). S4: −1.155 → −0.654 / −0.636. S1: +0.485 → +0.690 / +0.677. S1C: −0.722 → −0.594 / −0.709. Dashboard half-year 'walk-forward' bars use a flat 5% hurdle on the same unfunded NAV: 11/12 windows negative vs 7/12 at rf=0 (2020H1 −0.12 vs +1.04; 2022H1 −0.41 vs +1.51).
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one consistent convention. (a) Treat option P&L as an excess return: compute Sharpe/Sortino with rf=0 and label it 'Sharpe (excess P&L on $1M)'. Or (b) make NAV a funded account, NAV_t = NAV_{t-1}·(1 + r_{t-1}·Δt) + pnl_t, and keep the ^IRX hurdle; report cumulative/CAGR on that NAV and state that the cash leg is included. Apply the same convention in compute_crisis_performance (currently rf=0), the dashboard load_page4 recomputes (flat 5%) and the half-year chart. Remove the wrong 'ratio diverges' S3 footnote and show S3's Sharpe. Update README, dashboard and substack headline numbers. Test: compute_metrics on a zero-P&L NAV must give Sharpe 0 (or NaN), not a large negative number; and a funded-NAV test where a strategy earning exactly rf has Sharpe ≈ 0.

findings.title: Advertised ex-ante correlation 'Kelly netting' is mathematically a no-op (multiplier is always clipped to exactly 1.0)
findings.description: _corr_kelly_mult returns sqrt(2/(1+ρ)). For every ρ ∈ [−1, 1] that is ≥ 1 (and 1.414 when ρ is NaN→0). The geometric means are therefore ≥ 1, and .clip(0.5, 1.0) makes them exactly 1.0 on every day. Only _net_kelly_scale ever changes position size. The formula also points the wrong way for 'netting': it is largest when signals are uncorrelated and equals 1 at ρ=1. Still, ASSUMPTIONS, the dashboard's 'Step 7 Portfolio Kelly netting … ex-ante diversification sizing' and the README advertise it as a working risk control.
findings.evidence: From pass-1 P&L (engine code, scratchpad/bt): S1C multiplier min 1.1892 / max 2.2691, S3 min 1.1892, S4 min 1.2560. The fraction of days where clip(0.5, 1.0) ≠ 1.0 is 0.0000 for all three. sqrt(2/(1+ρ)) on ρ ∈ {−0.9, −0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0} = {4.47, 2.0, 1.41, 1.15, 1.03, 1.0}. Re-running S1C pass 2 with ONLY the net-Sharpe scale reproduces published pnl_s1c to max|diff| = 1.83e-09.
findings.proposed_fix: Either delete the correlation term and every claim about it (ASSUMPTIONS, the dashboard improvements list, README C13 'portfolio Kelly'), or implement a real risk-budgeting rule. Example: scale each sleeve by min(1, target_vol / trailing_portfolio_vol_contribution), or use mult_i = sqrt(1/(1 + Σ_j max(ρ_ij, 0))) so that positive correlation reduces size. Add unit tests: for two identical P&L series (ρ=1) the multiplier must be < 1; for uncorrelated series it must be 1; and pass 2 must differ from a net-Sharpe-only run when correlations are high.

findings.title: Delta-hedge costs skip the opening hedge and the closing unwind, and charge a rebalance on exit day that never happens
findings.description: Hedge slippage is charged only as SLIPPAGE_PCT·|Δ_t − Δ_{t−1}|·S·n·100 on HOLD days. At entry, nothing is charged for putting on the Δ0 hedge. On the exit day the code charges a rebalance to Δ_t, which a closing trader never does, and then books nothing for flattening the hedge. The flattening is large: S1 exits at about 1 session to expiry, when an in-the-money straddle has |Δ| near 1. The engine's own 5 bp hedge-cost assumption is therefore under-applied.
findings.evidence: Instrumented replica of _simulate_straddle_pnl, whose S1 P&L reproduces the engine's +$693,938 and 54 trades exactly. Net under-charge = entry |Δ0| + exit |Δ_{t−1}| − the spurious exit-day |Δ_t − Δ_{t−1}|, at the engine's 5 bp. S1 $92,489; S1C $67,210 (pass-1 sizes); S4 $9,757; S2 $3,082. For scale, the trade logs show total charged slippage of S1 $244,474 and S1C $131,082.
findings.proposed_fix: In the ENTRY branch, add slip0 = SLIPPAGE_PCT·|prev_delta|·S·n·100 to entry costs. In the exit path (pos==0), replace slip_t with SLIPPAGE_PCT·|prev_delta|·S·n·100 (the unwind) and do not rebalance to delta_t. Record both in TradeRecord.slippage_cost. Test: with constant S and vol, one long straddle held k days must carry slippage equal to 5bp·(|Δ0| + Σ|ΔΔ| + |Δ_exit|)·S·n·100, computed by hand.

findings.title: Delta-hedged P&L leaves out financing of the option premium and the hedge (r·(ΔS−V) − q·ΔS)
findings.description: daily_pnl = direction·(V_t − V_{t−1} − Δ_{t−1}ΔS) has no carry term. A self-financing delta-hedged book also earns or pays r on its cash (−V + ΔS for a long straddle) and pays or receives the dividend on the stock hedge. Under BS this term is what makes the hedged P&L equal to ½ΓS²(dS²/S² − σ²dt). Leaving it out biases shorts (which should earn interest on premium received but also finance long-Δ hedges) and longs in opposite directions. With ^IRX at 5% in 2023-24 the bias is material.
findings.evidence: Replica accumulating direction·[r_{t−1}(−V_{t−1} + Δ_{t−1}S_{t−1}) − qΔ_{t−1}S_{t−1}]/252·n·100 over each signal's actual trades: S1 −$55,105 (S1's published P&L is too high by this much); S1C +$99,341 (too low); S4 +$9,962; S2 −$47.
findings.proposed_fix: Add fin_t = direction·(r_{t−1}·(Δ_{t−1}·S_{t−1} − V_{t−1}) − q·Δ_{t−1}·S_{t−1})·Δt·n·100 to raw_pnl_t, with Δt = 1/252 to match the T_rem clock, and record it as a separate 'financing' field in TradeRecord. Do the same in delta_hedger.pnl_total, or document that it is an unfunded MTM. Test: in a synthetic BS world with constant σ equal to realised σ, the average daily hedged P&L including financing must be ≈ 0 (|mean| < 3·SE over many paths). Without the term it drifts by about rV.

findings.title: S3 proxy drops the exit-day P&L and charges zero exit cost, because it reads the exit day's kelly, which is 0
findings.description: _simulate_s3_pnl sizes each day as notional = k·nav with k = kelly on that day. On the exit day the signal is flat, so strength = kelly = 0. The overnight Δz exposure the position carried into that close books $0, exit_cost = S3_PROXY_COST·0 = $0, and the TradeRecord stores kelly_frac = 0. The straddle simulator correctly fixes size at entry; S3 does not. S3 is the one signal the project calls the 'survivor', so its headline figures (+$23,212, 73% win) are affected.
findings.evidence: From the re-run's signals: all 22 S3 exits have s3_kelly = 0.0; sum of S3 exit_cost in the published pkl = 0.0; recorded kelly_frac values = {0.0}. Engine re-run with a fixed simulator that holds k_entry and books exit-day Δz plus exit cost (scratchpad/bt/s3fix.py): S3 total +$23,212 → +$20,157 (−13%), win rate 72.7% → 77.3%; portfolio P&L −$261,206 → −$262,224, NAV $737,776, Sharpe −1.802.
findings.proposed_fix: Store k_in = kelly at entry and use notional = k_in·nav (optionally × the pass-2 multiplier captured at entry) for every holding day, including the exit day, and for exit_cost. Record kelly_frac = k_in. Test: with a hand-built z path where z jumps by +1 on the exit day, the exit-day P&L must equal k_in·nav·1·S3_Z_SCALE − exit cost, and exit_cost must be > 0.

findings.title: C7 attribution charges theta at 1/252 per session on a calendar-day clock and omits vanna/volga: the cumulative residual is larger than the total P&L
findings.description: T_rem decays on calendar time (days_elapsed/365.25), so Friday→Monday removes 3 days of time value. Yet pnl_theta = θ_{t−1}/252, a flat one-session charge. The weekend decay lands in the 'residual'. The Taylor expansion also stops at Γ and ν: vanna (∂²V/∂S∂σ·dSdσ) and volga (½∂²V/∂σ²·dσ²) are missing, and in 2020, with 10-20 pt VIX moves, they dominate the residual. The published 'hedge efficiency 0.016' (Var ratio) hides that the cumulative residual (−$182) exceeds the entire 2020 P&L (+$175).
findings.evidence: (1) Pure-BS Monte Carlo (200 GBM paths, σ = 20% constant, K = S0 = 3257.85, T = 1y, business-day calendar), using the module's own _bs_straddle_* functions: Var(resid)/Var(total) with the code's θ/252 = 0.1411; with θ·(T_{t−1} − T_t) = 0.0079. Mean residual on Mondays −1.66 vs +0.50 on other days. (2) Shipped delta_hedge_2020.parquet: mean residual_a by gap — 1-day −0.01, 3-day −3.58, 4-day −2.67. Adding calendar theta + vanna + volga: Var ratio 0.0164 → 0.0001, Σresid −182.2 → −9.6 (total P&L +175.4), and on 2020-03-16 resid −51.6 → −2.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Use pnl_theta = θ_{t−1}·(T_rem_{t−1} − T_rem_t) (a consistent clock). Add pnl_vanna = vanna_{t−1}·dS·dσ and pnl_volga = ½·volga_{t−1}·dσ², with straddle vanna = −2e^{−qT}n(d1)d2/σ and volga = vega·d1·d2/σ. Report the cumulative residual alongside the variance ratio, and rename 'hedge efficiency' to 'unexplained-variance ratio'. Test: a pure-BS path with constant σ must give Var(resid)/Var(total) < 0.02 and no weekday pattern.

findings.title: C7 Run B uses a PDV model fitted on 2010–2025 (including 2020) and is described as 'over-hedging', although its hedge is identical to Run A
findings.description: run_simulation loads data_store/pdv_model.pkl, whose coefficients were fitted on the full sample. The backtest engine itself rejects this as look-ahead ('pickled full-sample PDVModel (coefficients contaminated by future data — look-ahead bias)'). The module docstring still promises 'Zero look-ahead guarantee'. Separately, Run B changes only the vega attribution (pnl_vega_b = ν·(σ_PDV/σ_ATM)·dσ); the delta hedge is the same, and cum_pnl_b == cum_pnl_a by construction, as a test asserts. The report's 'Run B … over-hedge by 1.65×, worsening efficiency 0.016 → 0.303' therefore describes a re-labelled residual, not a hedge. The 1.65× and 91.6% figures are full-sample look-ahead values.
findings.evidence: pickle.load(pdv_model.pkl)._X.index spans 2010-02-02 → 2025-12-29 (4,002 rows, including all of 2020). delta_hedge_2020.parquet on 2020-03-16: sigma_pdv = 0.9158, sigma_atm = 0.554, pdv_ratio = 1.653. test_delta_hedger.py:536 asserts cum_pnl_a == cum_pnl_b.
findings.proposed_fix: Build Run B's σ_PDV with the engine's walk-forward PDVLinear (fit on returns strictly before 2020-01-01; reuse BacktestEngine._build_walkforward_pdv_vol logic). Change the report and HONEST_FAILURES text to 'PDV-scaled vega attribution explains less variance' and drop 'over-hedge'. If a real PDV hedge is intended, implement one (e.g., vega-hedge ratio from σ_PDV) and compare hedged P&L variance. Test: assert the PDV model used for 2020 has a training end date < 2020-01-01.

findings.title: README and Substack still print the pre-C21 S1/S1C figures (+$463K, −$404K, −$333K, −$99K, top-5 = 73%)
findings.description: The C21 re-run changed S1 to +$693,938 and S1C to −$599,995, and the README headline block (lines 35-36) was updated. The 'centrepiece' paragraph and the Substack article, which carry the core thesis, still quote the old numbers. README line 57 contradicts README line 35 on the same page.
findings.evidence: From data_store/backtest/full_results.pkl: S1 total +$693,938 (text says +$463K); S1C −$599,995 (text −$404K); worst S1 trade 2020-02-21→2020-03-17 −$299,415 (text −$333K); S1 2022 P&L −$74,670 (text −$99K); top-5 trades = 52.5% of S1 profit (text 73%). 53/54 short is still correct.
findings.proposed_fix: Regenerate the narrative numbers from the pkl (ideally a script that prints every figure quoted in README/substack), then fix README:57, 59 and substack:76-79. Better, add a test that parses the README/substack figures and compares them to full_results.pkl within rounding, so future re-runs cannot leave the prose stale. Any other numeric fix in this report will change these again.

findings.title: The 'Walk-Forward 6-Month OOS' Sharpe on the site is an in-sample slice at a flat 5% hurdle, and the engine's walk-forward classifier retrain does nothing
findings.description: The dashboard chart titled 'Walk-Forward Sharpe — 6-Month OOS Windows' slices the single full-period equity curve by half-year and subtracts a flat 5%. Nothing is re-fitted and nothing is out of sample. The engine's real walk_forward_validation retrains the C8 classifier per window (≈6 min each under load), but run() always passes precomputed_regimes=rule_regimes, and SignalEngine.generate ignores clf whenever precomputed_regimes is given. The retrain is pure cost and its docstring ('Re-train C8 classifier…') is false. _build_walkforward_regimes (95 lines) is never called, and run() still unpickles the classifier through _load_clf() only to ignore it.
findings.evidence: Single window 2020-01-01..06-30 (scratchpad/bt/wf1.py): retrained clf vs clf=None gives max|nav diff| = 0.0, regime diffs 0, Sharpe 0.9303 vs 0.9303; the retrain took 351.8 s. For the same half-year, the dashboard-style slice Sharpe (flat 5%) is −0.12 while the engine's WF-window Sharpe is +0.93. Dashboard half-year counts: 11/12 negative at the flat 5% vs 7/12 at rf=0. grep shows no caller of _build_walkforward_regimes.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the dashboard chart to 'Half-year sub-period Sharpe (in-sample, single run)', use the same rf convention as the headline, or publish the engine's actual walk-forward table. In the engine, drop the classifier retrain from walk_forward_validation (or actually use it when a flag like use_classifier=True is set). Delete _build_walkforward_regimes and skip _load_clf when precomputed regimes are used. Test: walk_forward_validation must not call _retrain_classifier unless the classifier is consumed.

findings.title: HTML report: wrong Sharpe label, charts and tables miss the portfolio legs, portfolio trade stats mix in research signals
findings.description: (a) The KPI and metrics table say 'Sharpe (5% rf)' / 'rf = 5%', but the metric uses per-date ^IRX. (b) The equity and contribution charts and the per-signal table show S1/S2/S3/Combined; the portfolio sleeves S1C and S4 are absent (SIGNAL_COLORS has no s1c/s4), while the S1 reference line (NAV $1.69M) dominates the chart. (c) Portfolio win_rate/n_trades/avg_pnl_per_trade are computed over self.all_trades, which includes the S1, S2 and Combined research trades. (d) The WF heading says 2019–2025, but the last window is 2024-07..2024-12. (e) C7 numbers (0.016, 0.303, 91.6%, 55.4%) are hard-coded rather than read from the parquet. (f) The monthly heatmap's pct_change drops January 2018 (+0.49%). (g) 'Total Gross P&L' labels a net-of-cost column.
findings.evidence: pkl metrics: n_trades 292, win_rate 0.455, avg_pnl −1,806. Portfolio-only (S1C+S3+S4): 141 trades, win 0.397, avg −5,555 per full-size sleeve. Jan-2018 NAV return +0.486% is missing from the heatmap (first bar is 2018-02-28). Code references as listed.
findings.proposed_fix: Label the Sharpe per the convention chosen in backtest-sharpe-double-counts-rf. Plot and tabulate S1C/S3/S4 as the portfolio, with S1/S2/Combined greyed as references (add colors). Compute portfolio trade stats from the portfolio signals only, e.g., compute_metrics(..., trade_log=[t for t in all_trades if t.signal in ('s1c','s3','s4')]). Derive the WF heading and C7 figures from the data. Seed the monthly series with initial capital. Test: the rendered report contains 'S1C' and 'S4', and the portfolio n_trades equals the sum of the three sleeves.

findings.title: The engine never expires a straddle: T_rem floors at 1 day and positions can be held for months with gamma but no theta
findings.description: After about 21 sessions, T_entry − (days_biz+1)/252 goes negative and T_rem is clamped at 1/365 indefinitely. The same stale-strike straddle keeps being marked at 1 day to expiry, so each day's hedged P&L is pure ½ΓdS² gamma with no theta (T never moves). This is the same class of defect as the C18 'marked past expiry' bug. S1/S1C/S2/S4 stay within expiry only because their signal max_hold values (21/10/15) happen to fit. The Combined reference series exceeds it, and any future signal or tenor change would silently repeat C18.
findings.evidence: Published trade log: Combined max holding 83 business days; 181 Combined days held beyond 21 sessions with P&L +$15,786 on those days. Other signals' max bdays: S1 20, S1C 20, S4 14, S2 9.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute expiry at entry (entry_date + tenor calendar days, or n_sessions = round(tenor×252/365)). When reached, settle at intrinsic |S−K|, close the trade (and roll to a new ATM straddle if the signal is still on). Add an assert/log if T_rem hits the floor while in_trade. Test: a position held 60 sessions must produce ≥ 2 TradeRecords with distinct strikes and no day marked at the 1/365 floor.

findings.title: Pricing rate falls back to 4.5% (not the prior day's rate) on dates missing from ^IRX; seven March-2020 days are missing because non-positive yields are dropped
findings.description: r_t = r.get(date, R_BACKTEST) uses a scalar 4.5% on any date not in the rate series, instead of forward-filling. The downloader filters close > 0, so the 7 sessions of 2020-03-19..27, when bills yielded about 0%, are missing. Those days would be priced at 4.5% instead of ~0%. compute_metrics does ffill, so the hurdle is unaffected. No published-signal position was open on those days, so the headline numbers are unchanged, but the defect is latent.
findings.evidence: Re-run: 7 signal dates are missing from the rate series: 2020-03-19, -20, -23, -24, -25, -26, -27. Positions open on those dates: S1 0, S1C 0, S4 0, S2 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Before the loop, r_series = r.reindex(position.index).ffill().fillna(self.r). Keep zero or negative ^IRX prints, clipped at 0 for pricing, instead of dropping them in download_tbill_rate. Test: a rate series with a gap must give r_t equal to the last observed value on the gap dates.

findings.title: Trade log omits the trade still open at the end, and sizing/margin keep using $1M after sleeve NAV has fallen
findings.description: (a) A trade open on the last date is never appended, so per-signal total_pnl/n_trades (which feed README) disagree with the NAV sleeves. (b) nav_const sizes every entry and computes the short-margin cap off $1M even after a sleeve has lost 60%. The comment 'No compounding — conservative' is untrue after losses: effective leverage on remaining equity rises about 2.5× for S1C, and the margin cap is not checked against real equity.
findings.evidence: S4 opened on 2025-03-24; nav_s4 P&L −$206,834 vs trade-log/README −$206,437 (−$397 entry cost missing). S1C sleeve NAV ends at $400,005 while sizing and margin still use $1,000,000.
findings.proposed_fix: At loop end, if in_trade, append a TradeRecord marked open=True (exit_date = last date, MTM), and report closed and open P&L separately. For sizing, either document it as fixed-notional (not 'conservative') or size and margin-check off each sleeve's running NAV shifted by 1 day. Test: the sum of TradeRecord net_pnl per signal must equal that sleeve's NAV P&L.

findings.title: C21 regression tests grep the source or re-implement the logic; attribution tests are tautological; key P&L paths are untested
findings.description: The T_rem fix is 'tested' by a BS-pricing monotonicity check that never calls the engine, plus a source-string grep for 'T_entry - (days_biz + 1) / TRADING_DAYS'. A harmless refactor breaks the grep, and a behavioural regression passes the other test. The ^IRX span check is re-implemented inside the test instead of calling engine code (it is inline in run()). The attribution-identity tests cannot fail, because the residual is defined as the remainder. test_delta_hedger's docstring promises a Var(resid_B) < Var(resid_A) test that does not exist. test_zero_kelly_no_contracts asserts only isinstance. Nothing covers the S3 exit day, hedge unwind cost, the correlation multiplier, or attribution quality in a pure-BS world. Each of those hides a bug reported above.
findings.evidence: A behavioural check that should replace the grep passes on current code: constant S=4000, flat 20% vol, long straddle held 6 sessions → engine gross −14,330.34 = (V(30/365 − 6/252) − V(30/365))·n·100 = −14,330.34. In-scope suite: 110 passed (WF deselected) in the scratch copy.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the grep with the behavioural decay test above. Extract the span check into a function (e.g., _validate_rate_series) and test it directly. Add: a pure-BS attribution residual test (<2% variance); an S3 exit-day P&L/cost test; hedge entry/unwind cost tests; a correlation-multiplier test (<1 at ρ=0.9); and a README-numbers-match-pkl test.

findings.title: HONEST_FAILURES and module docs contain claims that are no longer true
findings.description: HONEST_FAILURES says 'cumulative return is positive' and 'portfolio profit is dominated by the COVID-2020 window; ex-crisis the portfolio is roughly flat'. The portfolio is −26.1% cumulative, and the three crisis windows are each only +2.2 to +2.6%. The list is referenced only by a length-check test. ASSUMPTIONS advertises the no-op correlation netting. delta_hedger promises zero look-ahead while using the full-sample PDV. run_backtest's usage says cd "Volatility Trading System".
findings.evidence: compute_crisis_performance on the parquet: COVID_2020 +2.56%, FedHikes_2022 +2.27%, Tariffs_2025 +2.23%, against a −26.12% cumulative return. grep: HONEST_FAILURES is used only in test_backtest_engine.py:576.

checked_ok: Reproducibility: re-running BacktestEngine().run() on 2015-01-01..2025-03-24 DB data in the private copy reproduces data_store/backtest/full_results.parquet bit-for-bit (max |diff| ≤ 4e-9 on every NAV/P&L column, all position and regime columns identical) in about 4 s: NAV $738,794.35, Sharpe −1.7988, MaxDD −31.54%, cumulative −26.12%, ann. −4.13%, Calmar −0.131.

Per-signal headline numbers match the pkl: S1 +$693,938 / Sharpe 0.485 / 75.9% win / 54 trades; S1C −$599,995 / −0.722 / 36.4% / 88; S3 +$23,212 / 72.7% / 22; S4 −$206,437 / −1.155 / 25.8% / 31. README and dashboard headline values equal the engine output. The disagreements are the stale S1 narrative paragraph and the conventions reported as findings.

The C21 T_rem fix is behaviourally correct: a constant-spot, flat-vol long straddle held 6 sessions books exactly (V(T0−6/252) − V(T0))·n·100 = −$14,330.34 in the engine. The first holding day now decays.

The ^IRX span guard works: 1,809 real rows cover 2018-01-02..2025-03-24, decimal units (0.01378 on 2018-01-02), mean 2.40%. The discount-yield-vs-money-market convention difference is ≤ ~0.13%/yr and negligible for Sharpe.

Signal/trade timing is look-ahead-free: SignalEngine shifts features and regimes by 1 day, so the position on day t uses t−1 close information and trades execute at the close of t (a 1-session lag). S3 P&L starts the session after entry.
Every signal date is present in both the SPX and VIX tables (0 gaps). VIX9D/VIX/VIX3M/VIX6M have no NaNs in the window, so the 20% fallback vol never fires.

BS straddle value, delta e^{−qT}(2N(d1)−1), gamma, vega and theta (including r/q terms) in delta_hedger match textbook call+put sums. _straddle_vega matches 2× call vega. Total-variance VIX interpolation is correct. K_ENTRY 3257.85 equals the SPX close on 2020-01-02.

The bid-ask assumption is reasonable in calm/normal markets: measured half-spread for 20-40d near-ATM SPX options in the DB's 2026 snapshots is 0.04-0.19 vol pts per leg (median $0.70-$2.70 wide), against the engine's 0.15 vol pts per leg one-way. It does not widen in crises (a caveat, not a defect).

Portfolio aggregation is P&L-averaged fixed-notional sleeves, (S1C+S3+S4)/3 on sleeves sized off $1M, with returns taken as pct_change of the summed NAV. This is internally consistent (no NAV averaging, no rebalancing); sum of daily_pnl = −$261,206.

compute_metrics: Sortino uses the correct target downside deviation; max drawdown and duration (1,729 sessions) are computed correctly; CAGR is annualised over 1,807 returns with 252; the sqrt(252) Sharpe annualisation is consistent with the daily data.

Margin cap 20%·K·100 per short straddle is a reasonable approximation of CBOE SPX naked-straddle margin (~15% of underlying + premium). No S1/S1C/S4 entry was forced to 1 contract by zero Kelly; S2 had 1.
Crisis-window claims on the dashboard ('COVID, Fed, Tariffs all small +') are correct: +2.56%, +2.27%, +2.23%.
